title: ChaosScenarioFile
description: A single chaos scenario file. Lives under integration-test-data/chaos/scenarios/. Defines a chaos-injected test that every SDK CI can run identically via the shared launcher.

function.description: Logical grouping of tests, by parallel with tests/eval/<function>.yaml. Usually 'sse_resilience' for chaos.

expectations.description: Time-bounded assertions. Each MUST have within_ms — assertions check during chaos, not just at final state.

sdk.description: Which SDK runs the test. 'any' means the same scenario applies to every SDK.

topology.description: Rig topology. 'single' (default, original suite) — one upstream behind the sse/http proxies. 'failover' — one fixture upstream behind TWO HTTP proxies (primary+secondary); the SDK is configured with both URLs and toxics target the primary leg. 'ordering' — TWO fixture upstreams at divergent generations (see 'upstreams'); the SDK is configured with both and must end up holding the higher generation.

upstreams.description: Two-upstream layout for topology=ordering. The runner stands up one api-delivery fixture per entry, each pinned to its 'generation' via FIXTURE_GENERATION, and points the SDK at primary then secondary.

generation.description: Meta.generation this upstream serves (FIXTURE_GENERATION). Higher is strictly newer.

sse_endpoint.description: Whether SSE goes through the chaos proxy or direct to api-delivery.

http_endpoint.description: Whether HTTP polling goes through the chaos proxy or direct. Defaults to 'direct'. 'failover' — route HTTP through the primary+secondary proxy pair (topology=failover/ordering).

wall_clock_seconds.description: Max wall-clock seconds the test runner should keep the process up. Default 30s per the plan.

user_callback.description: Inject user-callback behavior. Used by scenario 10.

expected_state_on_start.description: Sanity assertion before chaos injection. Optional.

at_ms.description: When to apply this step, in ms relative to test start. Default 0 (immediately).

clear.description: Remove an earlier-injected toxic by name.

process.description: Out-of-band process action: kill/restart the proxy itself. Used by scenario 9.

inject.description: Either a convenience alias (one of the *_after_ms / *_ms / etc. shortcut keys) or a low-level toxiproxy 'toxic' spec.

name.description: Optional name so a later 'clear' step can remove this toxic.

proxy.description: Which named proxy to apply the toxic to. Default 'sse'. 'primary'/'secondary' name the failover-rig HTTP legs (topology=failover/ordering): 'primary' is the leg toxics target, 'secondary' is the fail-to leg.

sse_silent_stall_after_ms.description: Convenience: server stops sending bytes after N ms. Maps to toxiproxy 'timeout' toxic on the sse proxy.

sse_latency_ms.description: Convenience: add latency to every SSE packet.

sse_bandwidth_kbps.description: Convenience: throttle SSE bandwidth to N KB/s.

sse_down_ms.description: Convenience: close SSE connections and refuse new ones for N ms.

http_down_ms.description: Convenience: close HTTP connections and refuse new ones for N ms.

both_down_ms.description: Convenience: scenario 6 — kill both proxies for N ms.

sse_half_open_after_bytes.description: Convenience: scenario 7 — server returns 200 then closes after N bytes.

sse_http_status.description: Convenience: scenario 8 — force SSE endpoint to return this HTTP status indefinitely.

primary_refused_ms.description: Failover convenience (f01/f04): disable the primary HTTP proxy so the port refuses connections for N ms, then auto re-enable. Implies proxy=primary.

primary_hang_ms.description: Failover convenience (f02): apply a 'timeout' toxic to the primary HTTP proxy — the connection is accepted but never responds — for N ms. Implies proxy=primary.

primary_latency_ms.description: Failover/ordering convenience (f03/o03): add N ms of latency to the primary HTTP leg so the secondary wins the race. Implies proxy=primary.

toxic.description: Low-level toxiproxy toxic spec. Use only when no convenience alias above fits.

within_ms.description: Hard upper bound (ms from test start) by which the assertion MUST hold. Time-bounded assertions are checked during chaos, not at final state only.

assert.description: Assertion expression. Interpreted by the per-SDK runner; the schema only enforces presence.

must_hold_for_ms.description: Optional: once the assertion first holds, it must continue to hold for N ms (used for null-hypothesis steady-state assertions).
